name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index 136.0 in September, above the 135 Alert line
state: The FAO Food Price Index rose 1.5% in September to 136.0, 5.8% above a year earlier and above the 135 Alert line (published 8 Oct). Cereals and sugar led, on Black Sea logistics, dry weather and Hormuz shipping risk. The October figure is due on 6 Nov; no new reading as of 3 Nov.
for_you: Food import costs are high; supermarket prices tend to follow world prices with a delay of several months.
why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
